title: Etale pullback relation and its injective quotient presheaf
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $U,R,U'$ be schemes over $S$, and let $s,t:R\to U$ induce a monomorphism $(s,t):R\to U\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume that for every $S$-scheme $T$ the relation $x\sim_T y$ defined by $\exists r:T\to R,\ s r=x,\ t r=y$ is an equivalence relation on $U(T)$. Suppose $s,t$ and $g:U'\to U$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Set $A=U'\times_{g,U,s}R$ and $R'=A\times_{t\operatorname{pr}_R,U,g}U'$, and write $s',t':R'\to U'$ for its first and last projections. For every $T$, maps $T\to R'$ identify naturally with triples $(a,r,b)$ satisfying $s r=g a$ and $t r=g b$; the arrow $r$ is unique for given $(a,b)$. The morphism $(s',t'):R'\to U'\times_SU'$ is a monomorphism and identifies $R'(T)$ with the equivalence relation $a\sim'_T b\Longleftrightarrow g a\sim_T g b$. Both $s'$ and $t'$ are etale. Let $P(T)=U(T)/{\sim_T}$ and $P'(T)=U'(T)/{\sim'_T}$, with restrictions induced by precomposition, and let $h_U(T)=U(T)$ and $h_{U'}(T)=U'(T)$. The quotient maps $q:h_U\to P$ and $q':h_{U'}\to P'$ are surjective on sections over every $T$. There is a natural transformation $v:P'\to P$ with $v_T([a])=[g a]$, and it is injective over every $T$. It satisfies $v q'=q h_g$, where $h_g:h_{U'}\to h_U$ is postcomposition by $g$.

source.place: Tag 02WT (lemma-pullback-etale-equivalence-relation); Groupoids Tags 02V8 (lemma-restrict-relation), 02V9 (definition-restrict-relation), and the presheaf relation calculation in the proof of Tag 045Z (lemma-quotient-pre-equivalence-relation-restrict).

proof.text: Work throughout over $S$, so $U(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,U)$. By the universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product], a map $T\to A$ is a pair $(a,r)$ with $g a=s r$, and a map $T\to R'$ is such a pair together with $b:T\to U'$ with $t r=g b$. Thus these are precisely the triples $(a,r,b)$ in the statement. Precomposition by $c:T_1\to T$ sends this triple to $(a c,r c,b c)$, proving the claimed natural identification. If $r_1,r_2$ have the same endpoints $g a,g b$, their composites with $(s,t)$ agree, so $r_1=r_2$ by its assumed monomorphism.

For fixed $T$ and $a,b\in U'(T)$, a triple exists exactly when $g a\sim_T g b$. Consequently $R'(T)$ identifies with this inverse-image relation. It is reflexive because $g a\sim_T g a$, symmetric because $g a\sim_T g b$ implies $g b\sim_T g a$, and transitive because $g a\sim_T g b\sim_T g c$ implies $g a\sim_T g c$. To check the monomorphism directly, take any $z_1,z_2:T\to R'$ with the same image in $U'\times_S U'$. Their first and last coordinates agree; the uniqueness of $r$ from Step 1 makes the middle coordinates agree too, and the two successive pullback universal properties give $z_1=z_2$. This holds for every test scheme and proves that $(s',t')$ is a monomorphism.

source.place: Tag 02V8 (lemma-restrict-relation), filling the omitted proof on test schemes

proof.text: The projection R′→A is a base change of g, and A→U′ is a base change of s; their composite s′ is etale. For t′ no reassociation is needed: A→R is a base change of g, hence etale, and its composite A→R→U with t is etale. The projection t′ is the base change of that composite along g, hence etale. These four base-change applications use clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]; the two composition applications use clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The forgetful functor Over S→Scheme preserves these pullback squares, so the Mathlib Etale base-change property applies to the underlying scheme morphisms.

If $x\sim_T y$ is witnessed by $r:T\to R$, then $x c\sim_{T_1}y c$ is witnessed by $r c$ for every $c:T_1\to T$. The triple description gives the identical assertion for $\sim'$. Thus the rules $P(c)([x])=[x c]$ and $P'(c)([a])=[a c]$ are well-defined; their identity and composition laws follow from those for precomposition. The maps $q_T(x)=[x]$ and $q'_T(a)=[a]$ commute with these restrictions. They are surjective since every class of a set quotient has a representative, including when the underlying set is empty. In Lean, evaluation preserves coequalizers. Compose its coequalizer comparison isomorphism with Types.coequalizerIso to identify each evaluated coequalizer with Function.Coequalizer. Its generating relation consists of the endpoint pairs of arrows to R. The assumed equivalence relation already contains these generators and, conversely, every relation witness is a generator. Thus Quot.eqvGen_exact and Equivalence.eqvGen_iff prove the equality-of-classes characterization; the evaluated projection is epi in Type and therefore surjective. The same argument applies to R′.

source.place: Tag 045Z (lemma-quotient-pre-equivalence-relation-restrict), presheaf calculation; preceding lemma-quotient-pre-equivalence proof and equation-quotient-presheaf

proof.text: Define $v_T([a])=[g a]$. If $a\sim'_T b$, Step 2 gives $g a\sim_T g b$, so this is well-defined. Conversely $v_T([a])=v_T([b])$ means $g a\sim_T g b$, since $\sim_T$ already is an equivalence relation, and Step 2 gives $a\sim'_T b$, hence $[a]=[b]$. This proves injectivity, with no injectivity or surjectivity assumption on $g$. For $c:T_1\to T$, both $P(c)v_T([a])$ and $v_{T_1}P'(c)([a])$ equal $[g a c]$, proving naturality. Finally $(v_Tq'_T)(a)=[g a]=(q_T(h_g)_T)(a)$ for every $a$, proving $v q'=q h_g$. Construct v by coequalizer.desc from yoneda.map g followed by q: the projection identities and coequalizer.condition supply its equalizing equation. The descent equation gives the formula on representatives. Sectionwise surjectivity reduces injectivity to those representatives and the two equality-of-classes characterizations.

lean.statement: theorem etale_pullback_relation_presheaf {S : Scheme.{u}} {R U U' : Over S} (s t : R ⟶ U) [Mono (prod.lift s t)] (hrel : ∀ T : Over S, Equivalence (fun a b : T ⟶ U ↦ ∃ r : T ⟶ R, r ≫ s = a ∧ r ≫ t = b)) (g : U' ⟶ U) [Etale s.left] [Etale t.left] [Etale g.left] : ∃ (s' t' : pullback (pullback.snd g s ≫ t) g ⟶ U') (r' : pullback (pullback.snd g s ≫ t) g ⟶ R), s' = pullback.fst (pullback.snd g s ≫ t) g ≫ pullback.fst g s ∧ t' = pullback.snd (pullback.snd g s ≫ t) g ∧ r' = pullback.fst (pullback.snd g s ≫ t) g ≫ pullback.snd g s ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (a : T ⟶ U') (r : T ⟶ R) (b : T ⟶ U'), (r ≫ s = a ≫ g ∧ r ≫ t = b ≫ g) ↔ ∃! z : T ⟶ pullback (pullback.snd g s ≫ t) g, z ≫ s' = a ∧ z ≫ r' = r ∧ z ≫ t' = b) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (a b : T ⟶ U') (r₁ r₂ : T ⟶ R), r₁ ≫ s = a ≫ g → r₁ ≫ t = b ≫ g → r₂ ≫ s = a ≫ g → r₂ ≫ t = b ≫ g → r₁ = r₂) ∧ Mono (prod.lift s' t') ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (a b : T ⟶ U'), (∃ z : T ⟶ pullback (pullback.snd g s ≫ t) g, z ≫ s' = a ∧ z ≫ t' = b) ↔ ∃ r : T ⟶ R, r ≫ s = a ≫ g ∧ r ≫ t = b ≫ g) ∧ (∀ T : Over S, Equivalence (fun a b : T ⟶ U' ↦ ∃ z : T ⟶ pullback (pullback.snd g s ≫ t) g, z ≫ s' = a ∧ z ≫ t' = b)) ∧ Etale s'.left ∧ Etale t'.left ∧ (∀ T : Over S, Function.Surjective ((coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t)).app (op T))) ∧ (∀ T : Over S, Function.Surjective ((coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s') (yoneda.map t')).app (op T))) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (a b : T ⟶ U), (coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t)).app (op T) a = (coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t)).app (op T) b ↔ ∃ r : T ⟶ R, r ≫ s = a ∧ r ≫ t = b) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (a b : T ⟶ U'), (coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s') (yoneda.map t')).app (op T) a = (coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s') (yoneda.map t')).app (op T) b ↔ ∃ z : T ⟶ pullback (pullback.snd g s ≫ t) g, z ≫ s' = a ∧ z ≫ t' = b) ∧ ∃ v : coequalizer (yoneda.map s') (yoneda.map t') ⟶ coequalizer (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t), (∀ (T : Over S) (a : T ⟶ U'), v.app (op T) ((coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s') (yoneda.map t')).app (op T) a) = (coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t)).app (op T) (a ≫ g)) ∧ (∀ T : Over S, Function.Injective (v.app (op T))) ∧ coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s') (yoneda.map t') ≫ v = yoneda.map g ≫ coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t)
